iconicAnchor.label: Sewn signatures cased into a crafted cover as a durable working book
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Library of Congress describes binding as an engineered relationship among sewn or glued text block, spine, boards, endpapers, and covering, with protection and usable opening as core purposes.

sources.title: Why We Bind
supports: Books with sewn signatures are assembled as a text block and cased into a cover and spine built from board and covering material.
A binding is functional engineering that protects pages while keeping the volume accessible to readers.

sources.title: The Fragility of Joints and Hinges
supports: Joints and hinges form the flexible structural connection where boards meet the spine and determine how a book opens.
Leather, vellum, textile, and paper are all established covering or structural materials whose wear reveals the book's construction.
